questions.q: What did milkmaids who caught cowpox turn out to be?
a: Immune to smallpox later in life
Carriers who spread smallpox to others
Resistant to all bacterial infections
Unable to pass immunity to their children
questions.why: Lesson 1 says exposure to the milder cowpox protected them, which inspired vaccination.

questions.q: What happens in your body when you get a vaccine?
a: A small dose triggers an immune response and memory cells
Antibiotics are injected to kill viruses directly
Your immune system is temporarily switched off
Your blood is filtered to remove all pathogens
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains a vaccine exposes you to a small dose so your body produces cells that kill the virus.

questions.q: What are the body's three immune responses, in order?
a: Physical barriers, innate immunity, adaptive immunity
Fever, inflammation, antibody production
Mucus, stomach acid, bone marrow
Innate immunity, vaccination, recovery
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists barriers that block pathogens, then innate immunity, then specialized adaptive immunity.

a: The immune system attacking the body's own cells
A virus that resists every known vaccine
An infection that spreads through the bloodstream
A condition where the body cannot make new cells
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a malfunctioning immune system can fight the body itself, as in type 1 diabetes or lupus.

questions.q: What did hepatitis-B vaccination appear to do to liver cancer rates?
a: Reduce them by more than 80 percent
Leave them unchanged over ten years
Cut them roughly in half
Increase them among older patients
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites an 80%+ drop in liver cancer after the vaccine became standard practice.
